result.description: Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API) lets businesses send and receive WhatsApp messages, templates, media and webhooks, and manage WABAs and phone numbers.
result.auth_detail: Direct developers use a System User access token, sent as a Bearer token. Tech Providers get per-customer Business Integration System User tokens by implementing Embedded Signup (Facebook Login for Business) and exchanging the returned code. The REST API docs fetched never use the word "OAuth". The code exchange is the standard OAuth2 authorization-code pattern, so oauth2 is inferred. Short-lived User tokens come from Facebook Login or the dashboard. Meta's separate MCP server uses OAuth explicitly.
result.access_detail: Anyone can register as a Meta developer, create an app and get a temporary token plus a test number for free. Production sending needs a business portfolio, a real phone number and permissions. Serving other businesses' accounts needs Advanced access via App Review and business verification, and Tech Provider status. I did not find business verification or pricing on the fetched get-started page. Meta charges per-message fees, which are not API-gated.
result.api_notes: Graph API REST at graph.facebook.com/vXX.X. It covers messages (text, media, templates, interactive), media, phone numbers, WABA and template management, business profile, QR codes, flows, analytics, and inbound webhooks. Message sending is limited by a 24-hour customer service window, templates and per-number rate limits.
result.blocker: Multi-tenant end-user connect needs Meta App Review (Advanced access), business verification and Embedded Signup or Tech Provider setup. Single-account use with a system user token works now. Messaging is constrained by the 24-hour window and template approval.
